subject: Reliability allowance & pro-rata remedy schedule — Finova SLA draft
messages:
From: Diane Peters <diane.peters@finova.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Finova Procurement <procurement@finova.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood SLA — initial comments and credit structure question

Michael — thanks for sending the SLA template. We reviewed the draft and have a couple of substantive items before we can circulate to our legal/procurement: 

1) Monthly remedy structure: your current draft lists a single monthly credit cap and a flat percent for any uptime shortfall. We'd like to propose a laddered approach so the incentive aligns with customer impact across small vs. severe degradation. Can you clarify if Redwood is open to graduated credits tied to bands (e.g., 99.9–99.5, 99.5–99.0, <99.0)?

2) Latency SLO: Finova relies on sub-250ms p95 for synchronous inference. The draft lists a 300ms target — can you provide data on p95 performance for our projected throughput (see attached usage profile)?

3) Partial-month pro-rata: if we exercise a ramp or terminate mid-month, how will credits be calculated? Procurement needs explicit language.

Attached: Finova side redlines and our monthly usage profile. Can we schedule a quick sync this week to work through numeric proposals?

Thanks,
Diane Peters
Head of Platform Partnerships
Finova Analytics

Attachments: finova-sla-comments.docx (13KB), usage-profile-june.csv (4KB)

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Diane Peters <diane.peters@finova.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood SLA — initial comments and credit structure question

Diane — appreciate the thoughtful review and the profile. Quick answers up front, and then a proposed path: 

A) Laddered credits: yes, we can do a graduated monthly remedy ladder. We typically avoid open-ended liability but are happy to define bands with a monthly cap and a per-band percentage. Instead of a single flat percentage we propose a small "reliability allowance" concept: a protected buffer (e.g., 0.05% uptime), then three bands with increasing credit percentages.

B) Latency: Ben will pull the p95 numbers for your projected concurrency. Anecdotally we hit ~180–220ms p95 on the model family you selected at modest concurrency, but batched inference and very high KC (key-cache) reuse can push it higher. We'll provide empirical profiles within 24 hours.

C) Pro-rata: we can accept explicit pro-rata wording for partial months; propose the same calendar-day-weighting language most enterprise contracts use.

Next step: propose a short call Monday (20–30m) to align on band breakpoints and the monthly cap. If you prefer numbers in doc first, we can circulate a redline with proposed percentages and caps and a worked example for a 30-day month. 

I'll attach a redline draft that frames the allowance and band ladder. Marissa will own the contract language; Ben will own the operational numbers.

—Michael
Michael Grant
VP, Sales — North America
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-sla-draft-v3.pdf (7KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Redwood SLA — initial comments and credit structure question

Folks — dug into Finova's usage profile (thanks Diane) and ran a few sims on our staging fleet. Notes below we should surface to them: 

- Baseline latency (model x-large, mixed KV cache): p50 ~55ms, p95 ~190–230ms at 40 concurrent streams with continuous batching. At 200 concurrent streams (bursty), p95 moves toward 320–420ms unless we enable aggressive batching limits: in practice we can keep <300ms p95 up to ~120 concurrents with the planned instance mix.

- Proposal for laddered credits: 
  * Reliability allowance (no-credit zone): 0.05% monthly (to cover transient infra noise and planned minor ops)
  * Band A (uptime 99.95–99.50%): credit = 5% of monthly fee for that month
  * Band B (99.49–99.00%): credit = 15% of monthly fee
  * Band C (<99.00%): credit = 40% of monthly fee, with a point to discuss absolute cap (we propose monthly cap = 200% of monthly fee)

- Latency SLO: propose p95 <= 250ms for synchronous endpoints as the contractual SLO; include an operational carveout for batch jobs (asynchronous) and scheduled maintenance windows. If Finova needs a stricter p95 we can commit but would require reserved capacity pricing.

- Pro-rata calculation: day-weighted by total calendar days in the month. We should add an example in the redline.

I recommend we present these numbers on the call and capture Finova's comfort with the monthly cap and the reliability allowance. 

—Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Diane Peters <diane.peters@finova.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Finova Procurement <procurement@finova.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood SLA — ladder proposal and latency SLO

Thanks for the quick follow-up and the concrete bands. A few counterpoints from procurement/legal: 

1) Monthly cap: Finova prefers a fixed cap at 100% of the monthly fee. The 200% cap Ben proposed is a non-starter for us.

2) Reliability allowance: procurement is okay with a small no-credit buffer, but they want the allowance to be explicit that it excludes planned maintenance >30 minutes if notified 72 hours in advance. Otherwise we risk silent carveouts.

3) Latency SLO: the 250ms p95 is closer to our needs; however, we need an explicit statement on how concurrent bursts are handled and whether reserved capacity with guaranteed p95 is an add-on. Finova can consider reserved instances if Redwood provides a binding throughput guarantee.

4) Example: please include a worked example for a partial month termination where the incident spans the boundary (we want to ensure credits are apportioned correctly).

We are available Tue 22 Jun 10:00–10:30 PT for a call to align.

Best,
Diane
Head of Platform Partnerships, Finova

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Diane Peters <diane.peters@finova.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood SLA — ladder proposal and latency SLO (summary & next steps)

Diane — thanks. Summary and next steps after internal sync: 

1) Monthly cap: we can accept Finova's request to lower the absolute cap to 100% of the monthly fee, provided we tighten the Band C threshold language and add a 6-month mutual exit right if severe, sustained outages occur. We'll capture both in the redline.

2) Reliability allowance: we'll keep the 0.05% allowance and explicitly exclude planned maintenance >30 minutes with 72h notice. We'll also include a brief definition of what counts as "planned" vs. "emergency" maintenance.

3) Latency: we confirm p95 <= 250ms as a synchronous SLO for standard hosted endpoints at the assumed concurrency profile. If Finova needs binding throughput (concurrency) guarantees, we'll add a reserved capacity addendum at a tiered price. We'll include a worked example showing behavior at 60 concurrent streams vs. 180.

4) Pro-rata and boundary incidents: Marissa will draft the example clause and a numeric example for partial-month termination/incidents; Ben will attach the empirical latency tables.

5) Call: we are confirmed for Tue 22 Jun 10:00 PT — I'll send the calendar invite and a DocuSign link once we exchange the redline.

Appreciate the constructive dialogue — we want to keep this simple and predictable for both sides.

—Michael
VP, Sales — North America
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood-sla-draft-v3.pdf, example-pro-rata.xlsx (stub)
